newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Justice closely monitors state tobacco suits.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Justice closely monitors state tobacco suits.

text.p: A U.S. Justice Department official said Thursday it has closely monitored the state lawsuits against tobacco firms over smoking-related illnesses, but he did not know if it would get involved in the cases.

"We have not ... entered those lawsuits as a party. But we have carefully and closely monitored what has gone on in those lawsuits pursuant to our other responsibilities and investigations," Acting Deputy Attorney General Seth Waxman said.

Five Democratic senators Tuesday asked that Attorney General Janet Reno have the Justice Department file suit against the tobacco companies to recoup the federal government's cost of treating smoking-related illnesses.

Waxman said the state lawsuits seek to recover costs under the federal Medicaid law, and that the law specifically gives the states the legal standing to bring liability lawsuits seeking damages against third-parties.

"The statute does not give the federal government the authority to bring such lawsuits because the way the statutory scheme works recoveries that are obtained by the states will be shared pro rata with the United States," he said.
But Waxman refused to say that the Justice Department definitely would not get involved in the matter.
"Whether there might be some mechanism for us to get involved I don't have the jurisprudence to give you a categorical answer," he said at the weekly Justice Department news briefing.
"But in light of the way that the pro rata reimbursement mechanism works, and in light of the progress of the suits, we have not determined that we ought to," he said.
